name: Idi Amin
summary: Army officer who seized power in Uganda in a 1971 coup and ruled as military head of state until 1979. His government expelled most of the country's Asian population in 1972 and transferred their businesses and property to supporters, ran a state security service that tortured and killed suspected opponents, and governed by decree and a military council. He praised Hitler, attacked Israel, and in 1975 called for Israel's expulsion from the UN.

population-transfer.rationale: Ordered the 1972 expulsion of Asians from Uganda, announced 4 August with a deadline of about three months; tens of thousands left, and the stated reason was that they were sabotaging the economy.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Defended the expulsion as 'giving Uganda back to ethnic Ugandans', as quoted by Jorgensen (1981) in the Wikipedia article on the expulsion.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: In an October 1975 UN address he called for the expulsion of Israel from the UN and the extinction of Israel as a state, as excerpted by the Jewish Press. He also severed ties with Israel in 1972. The speech is known only from press excerpts.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Annexed part of Tanzania's Kagera Region in 1978, which Radio Uganda declared annexed, and in 1976 suggested parts of Kenya and Sudan were historically Ugandan before backing down.

force-without-un.rationale: Endorsed and sustained the 1978 invasion of Tanzania without any UN authorisation. Whether he personally ordered the first attack is disputed.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred: from his 1976 claim that parts of Kenya and Sudan were historically Ugandan. He did not state the general principle that a historical tie outweighs other peoples' present claims.

nation-first.rationale: Broke diplomatic ties with Britain and Israel in 1972, nationalised British-owned businesses, and turned to Libya and the Soviet Union for loans and arms rather than to Western partners.

political-violence-never.rationale: Came to power in a 1971 military coup and ruled through the State Research Bureau, whose torture and killings of suspected opponents were central to his rule.

revolution-justified.rationale: Took power by a military coup and presented it as ending corruption under the previous government. An army seizure of power is not a revolution, so the answer is low.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Created the State Research Bureau by decree, and its agents tortured and executed suspected dissidents; a 1974 commission blamed it for most disappearances.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: In February 1971 suspended parts of the constitution and gave military tribunals authority above civil law.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Ruled through a military Advisory Defence Council that he chaired, and described the military government as a temporary caretaker regime.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Declared himself president, commander-in-chief and chief of staff in February 1971, and chaired the Defence Council that governed the country.

strong-leader.rationale: Ruled by decree through a military council and was declared president for life in 1976. He also said 'Politics is like boxing: you try to knock out your opponents' (Palm Beach Post, January 1976, quoted on Wikiquote). He did not state the principle in these words.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Gave military tribunals authority above civil law and governed by decree, so he was not bound by the constitutional order he had suspended.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Governed mainly by decree: the 1972 expulsion was ordered by decree announced in a single address, and the Defence Council made decisions case by case.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The Defence Council declared him 'president for life' in June 1976, removing any term limit.

term-limits.rationale: The Defence Council declared him 'president for life' in June 1976, which rejects any limit on his tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Governed without an elected parliament after the 1971 coup; the Defence Council under his chairmanship made the decisions instead.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Expelled Asians on the basis of their origin, and filled the army with his own ethnic and regional groups while purging others.

property-fundamental.rationale: Seized businesses, farms and homes of Asians and Europeans in 1972 and reallocated about 5,655 firms and farms, mostly to individual supporters.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Expropriated and reallocated property in 1972 and nationalised British-owned businesses, reaching well beyond defence, justice and property protection.

public-ownership.rationale: Nationalised British-owned businesses in 1972, but then reallocated them to individual supporters rather than to public ownership.

empower-police-military.rationale: Expanded the army into the core of government and set up the State Research Bureau and the Public Safety Unit as security forces.

separate-church-state.rationale: Used state patronage of Islam through the Uganda Muslim Supreme Council and appointed its mufti. No stated view on separation.

more-religion-public.rationale: Used state patronage to draw Muslims into political power and to centralise the Muslim council, according to a scholarly chapter. No stated view on religion in public life.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Said the 1972 policy aimed to transfer economic control of Uganda into Ugandan hands, quoted by Jorgensen (1981) via the expulsion article. He treated economic control as the point of independence.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Inferred: from his reported approval of the Holocaust and his 1972 telegram to Kurt Waldheim praising Hitler's treatment of Jews (as reported by Wikipedia), which treats it as having happened. He made no recorded statement on whether it happened as historians describe.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Quoted (via Wolcott 2004, on Wikiquote) as saying that Hitler, though some thought him bad, was a great man. Constitutional antifascism is not addressed directly.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Justified the 1971 coup and his rule as removing corruption, and described his mission as leading the country out of 'corruption, depression and slavery' (1978 US Senate document, quoted on Wikiquote).

leader-cult.rationale: Gave himself grandiose public titles, such as 'His Excellency, President for Life, Field Marshal Al Hadji Doctor Idi Amin Dada', quoted from the Africana encyclopedia on Wikiquote.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Ruled without elections after the 1971 coup, presenting the military government as temporary pending elections that did not follow in his time in office.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Said the 1972 policy aimed to transfer economic control of Uganda into Ugandan hands, away from Asian and European owners, as quoted by Jorgensen (1981) via the expulsion article.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Launched the 1978 invasion of Tanzania and the annexation of the Kagera Salient, which was a war of aggression rather than defence against attack.

notes: Many of his public statements survive only as press reports or secondary quotations, and the text of his 1975 UN speech and the 1972 telegram could not be checked against a primary transcript (the UN record and press pages were unreachable). The initial order for the 1978 Kagera invasion is disputed. The extent of formal Islamisation policy is unclear from the sources reached. Most of his record concerns force, property and rule by decree; positions on the large majority of statements (e.g. markets, welfare, family, culture) have no recorded evidence and are left null.
